correctness.rationale: The exact density gives the corrected integral after the substitution \(y=-\log x\). The source's Eq. (5.8) still contains \(e^{-r y}\), so its replacement by the single gamma term in Eq. (5.9) is algebraically invalid. At \(\alpha=\beta=1\), \(p=1/2\), the printed series sums analytically to \(2\log2\), while direct integration gives \(2\log2-1\). The support \((0,1)\) makes the printed value impossible. The beta-one hypergeometric formula follows by the exact substitution \(u=x^\alpha\).
